evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 005 ER-01, which this claim commits to test.

Before: _assess samples evaluator_extension_present before creating outputs and only reports it in the JSON summary; assess runs to a scored verdict in a project with no evaluator extension (tests/test_runner.py::test_assess_success_names_only_written_files asserts success with evaluator_extension_present false). The clean-refusal channel already exists: pre-flight failures raise ValueError, main() prints 'refused: ...' to stderr and returns 2, with no traceback and no outputs.

Shipped refusal test: in a project with no .specify/extensions/evaluator, the stubbed assess exits 2 with a clean 'refused:' message naming spec-kit-evaluator and 'specify extension add spec-kit-evaluator', prints no JSON, and writes nothing (no .specify/extensions/aee tree, no evaluator dir created); independently probed against the real engine 1.5.0 with the same result (exit 2, only the input file present afterwards).

falsification_tests: Run assess in a project without .specify/extensions/evaluator and observe it score a verdict, write an assessment/evaluator-result/ledger/latest-pointer file, or refuse without naming spec-kit-evaluator and the install command.
claims.text: assess refuses when the spec-kit-evaluator extension is not installed in the project: with .specify/extensions/evaluator/ absent, the runner exits 2 before running the engine or writing any output, and the refusal message names the missing extension and how to install it (specify extension add spec-kit-evaluator), stating that composition through the evaluator extension is part of the standard flow.

boundary: scripts/python/run_aee.py _assess happy path; commands/speckit.aee.assess.md reporting guidance

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 005 ER-02, which this claim commits to test.

Baseline: the 1.3.0 suite (127 passed) pins the happy path end to end - outputs named only when written, verdict passthrough, evaluator_extension_present reporting, verdict display - across tests/test_runner.py, tests/test_p5_vocabulary.py, and tests/test_integration.py; the assess command document already recommends composition when the runner reports the extension present.

Full suite in the repo-pinned layout (pip install --require-hashes -r requirements/dev.txt; engine 1.5.0 from PyPI): 133 passed, including every pre-existing happy-path assess test (stubbed and real-engine) with unchanged outputs and evaluator_extension_present: true; scripts/check_install.py against the real spec-kit-evaluator v1.1.0 checkout prints PASS with the installed runner's assess exercised.

falsification_tests: With the evaluator extension installed, run the 1.3.0-era assess scenarios and observe any output field, exit code, or written file differ from the pre-change behavior other than the extension_version stamp.
claims.text: With the spec-kit-evaluator extension installed, assess behaves exactly as in 1.3.0 - same outputs, same exit-code passthrough, evaluator_extension_present: true in the JSON summary - and the assess command document presents composition through the evaluator extension as the standard next step when other evaluators ran at the same phase.

boundary: extension.yml requires.tools; README.md requirements and install sections; commands/speckit.aee.assess.md prerequisites; docs/usage.md

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 005 ER-03, which this claim commits to test.

Before: extension.yml declares spec-kit-evaluator required: false under an 'OPTIONAL for this adapter' comment; the README requirements table labels it 'Evaluator Contract (optional)', its paragraph says the extension 'is not a runtime dependency of this adapter', and its install block marks it '# Optional'; commands/speckit.aee.assess.md says it is 'not required to run assess'; docs/usage.md calls it optional - while scripts/check_install.py installs both extensions and asserts both enabled, so declaration and practice disagree.

Manifest and docs tests pass: extension.yml declares spec-kit-evaluator required: true at version >=1.0.0,<2 with the one-system comment; README requirements table/install, the assess command document, and docs/usage.md carry required-companion framing and the pinned negative strings ('Evaluator Contract (optional)', '**not** required to run assess', 'needed only for compose/report') are asserted absent.

falsification_tests: Parse extension.yml after the change and find spec-kit-evaluator required: false, or find optional/not-required framing for the evaluator extension in README.md, commands/speckit.aee.assess.md, or docs/usage.md.
claims.text: The pair is declared and taught as one system: extension.yml declares spec-kit-evaluator required: true (version >=1.0.0,<2), and the README requirements/install sections, the assess command document, and the usage docs present the evaluator extension as a required companion installed together with this adapter - no user-facing surface calls it optional or not-required.

boundary: scripts/check_install.py install flow and refusal exercise

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 005 ER-04, which this claim commits to test.

Before: check_install.py installs the evaluator extension first (specify extension add --dev) and asserts installed['evaluator']['enabled'] and installed['aee']['enabled'] before exercising operations, but never runs an operation with the evaluator extension absent, so runner-level absence was tolerated by the install check.

check_install.py run end to end against the real spec-kit-evaluator v1.1.0 tag checkout: PASS (exit 0) with the new absence exercise inside the flow - the evaluator directory is removed from the installed scratch project and the installed runner's assess must exit 2 naming spec-kit-evaluator and write no new assessment, alongside the pre-existing both-enabled assertion; the exercise is also pinned by a source test.

falsification_tests: Run check_install.py in a flow where the evaluator extension is missing or disabled and observe it print PASS, or remove the evaluator directory in its scratch project and observe the installed runner's assess succeed.
claims.text: check_install.py fails when the evaluator extension is absent or disabled: its install flow asserts both extensions are enabled, and it exercises the enforcement end to end - with the evaluator extension removed from the installed scratch project, the installed runner's assess exits 2 naming the missing extension, and any other outcome fails the script.
